name: api-endpoint
title: API endpoint
description: An API route as one row: the method as a label told apart by weight and outline, the path with its parameters quieter, a line on what it does and the auth it needs.
docs: method is GET, POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, drawn as a label in monospace whose fill, outline (thin, heavy or dashed) and weight tell the five apart in black and white (only DELETE borrows the destructive token). path is the route with its parameters written :id or {id} (a query string works too): fixed parts are set in a medium weight and the parameters in a quieter one, so the shape of the route reads at a glance. baseUrl is what the routes hang from; the copy button copies baseUrl + path, so the clipboard holds an address that works in a terminal (fullUrl and routeParts are exported if you need them). auth is the words (Bearer token, API key, OAuth 2 · orders:read), false says it needs nothing and leaving it out says nothing; screen readers hear Authentication: before it. deprecated strikes the route through and adds a Deprecated mark. With href the route is the row's one link and the whole row opens it, while the copy button stays a separate target. Every link and copy button names its route (GET /v1/orders, Copy URL of GET /v1/orders), so a screen reader listing them can tell the routes apart. A Server Component; labels carries the words, and labels.copy takes {method} and {path}.
